reports.name: Snn6
reports.note: SnTox6 (SnTox267) sensitivity gene near the distal end of 6AL, mapped in the ITMI population and delineated to a 3.2 cM interval between the EST-derived markers XBE424987 and XBE403326 (Gao 2015, PhD thesis; Gao et al. 2015 MPMI). Neither flanking marker could be placed on the reference (BE424987 has no match in the gene models; BE403326 matches only a 3B gene), so the interval shown is the distal part of 6AL covered by the EST markers of the same study that could be placed (BF145792 582.0, BE494057 585.4, BF428729 603.1, BE590952 612.3 Mb on RefSeq v1.0) to the end of 6A. Treat as an approximate region, not a mapped interval. Reported to be rare in hexaploid wheat, identified in synthetic wheat.
reports.evidence: Four of the nine PCR-based markers mapped within 10 cM of Snn6, with markers XBE424987 and XBE403326 immediately flanking the gene and delineating it to a 3.2 cM interval

reports.name: Snn7
reports.note: SnTox7 (SnTox267) sensitivity gene on 2DL. Interval from the flanking SSRs Xgdm6 and Xgwm349; peak at the cosegregating marker Xcfd44. Marker positions on IWGSC RefSeq v1.0 from Zhao et al. (2019) J Genet 98:69.
reports.evidence: The marker Xcfd44 cosegregated with Snn7, and the microsatellite markers Xgdm6 and Xgwm349 flanked Snn7 at distances of 0.9 and 1.8 cM, respectively

reports.name: Snn1-B2
reports.note: SnTox1 sensitivity gene; a second copy of Snn1 about 120 kb from Snn1-B1 on 1BS, present in some lines only. Interval shown is Snn1-B1 (TraesCS1B02G004100, 2.382 Mb) plus and minus 120 kb; the copy has no independent map position.
reports.evidence: some wheat lines possess two copies of Snn1 (designated Snn1-B1 and Snn1-B2) approximately 120 kb apart

reports.name: Snn3-B2
reports.note: Cloned. Second SnTox3 sensitivity gene on 5BS, a PK-MSP paralogue sharing 94.0% genomic identity with Snn3-B1. Absent from Chinese Spring, so it has no position in the reference assembly; present in Sumai 3, Julius, Mace and Norin61. Position shown is inferred: about 1 Mb distal to Snn3-B1 (7.090 Mb on RefSeq v2.1) on the short arm, shown as a 1 Mb window. A presence/absence KASP marker, Snn3-B2_P/A, is reported.
reports.evidence: Although the gene locations vary, these two genes were about 1 Mb apart, with Snn3-B2 being distal to Snn3-B1 on chromosome 5BS

reports.name: Snn5-B2
reports.note: SnTox5 sensitivity gene; a second Snn5 locus reported by Running (2022). No physical position available in the sources held here, so the gene is not placed; the chromosome is given as 4B by analogy with Snn5-B1 and should be confirmed from the original paper.

reports.name: Snn3-B1
reports.note: Cloned. SnTox3 sensitivity gene encoding a protein kinase-major sperm protein (PK-MSP), temporarily designated TaPKMSP-5B1. Chinese Spring gene TraesCS5B01G007900 (RefSeq v1.0 low-confidence annotation) = TraesCS5B02G007900LC = TraesCS5B03G0013500LC (RefSeq v2.1, Chr5B 7,090,022-7,092,940). A presence/absence KASP marker, Snn3-B1_P/A, is reported.
reports.evidence: A PK-MSP gene (TraesCS5B01G007900), which we temporarily designated as TaPKMSP-5B1, was identified in low-confidence annotations in the wheat Chinese Spring IWGSC RefSeq v1.0 genome assembly. A new ID (TraesCS5B03G0013500LC) was assigned to the same gene in the RefSeq v2.1 assembly.

reports.name: Snn5-B1
reports.note: Original mapping of the SnTox5 sensitivity gene, in the tetraploid LP749 population (Lebsock x PI 94749, 120 DH). Snn5 mapped 2.8 cM proximal to Xwmc349 (4B 640.98 Mb) and 13.3 cM distal to Xbarc163 and Xcfd22, which have no position on the reference; the proximal bound shown is Xbarc227 (567.20 Mb), the marker defining the 4BL-5 deletion breakpoint, since the paper places Snn5 in the most distal deletion bin of 4BL (about 15% of the arm). LOD 25.0 and PVE 63% are for the SnTox5-only strain Sn2000KO6-1; with the wild type Sn2000 the values are LOD 11.6 and PVE 37%. The SnTox5-Snn5 interaction is light dependent. Interval width 74 Mb: this is a chromosome region as the source reports it, not a fine-mapped locus, and should not be treated as one in co-localisation.
reports.evidence: The Snn5 locus mapped 2.8 cM proximal to the marker Xwmc349 and 13.3 cM distal to markers Xbarc163 and Xcfd22 ... all markers distal to Xbarc227, including Snn5, are probably located in the most distal deletion bin of 4BL

reports.name: QFcr.cg-3D

reports.name: QFcr.cg-2A
reports.note: QTL for Fusarium crown rot field resistance in the PAN 3471 / SST 087 doubled-haploid population, trial year 2022 (South Africa). Favourable allele from PAN 3471. Physical interval is the Chinese Spring (IWGSC RefSeq v1.0) span between the flanking DArT markers 1105077 (2A:42,194,565) and 3034278 (2A:698,281,086), taken from Martin et al. (2025) Table 4. "cg" denotes a QTL from the South African trials, "usq" from the Australian trial. The source reports an interval but no QTL peak, so no peak is stored; earlier versions of the atlas showed the interval midpoint here, which was not a reported position. REMOVED AS A POSITION: the two flanking markers lie 656 Mb apart on 2A, which cannot be a QTL confidence interval. Martin et al. note that some DArT markers lack a 100% BLAST hit on the target chromosome, so at least one flanking position is unreliable. The reported flanking positions were 42.195 Mb and 698.281 Mb; the locus is therefore recorded without a physical position until the figure or supplementary table that localises it is available.
